input.safetyLimits: No flashing lights, loud sounds, or physical construction.

result.message: Here are three distinct digital trails to help you test how movement and space relate to anxiety and uncertainty.
result.reason: Three eligible digital experiments fit the beginner skill level, 15-minute time limit, and safety constraints without requiring physical materials or coding.

experiments.title: Space between
experiments.researchQuestion: How does adjusting the gap between two moving shapes change the feeling of closeness or distance in your scene?
experiments.conceptConnection: Testing the space between elements can help examine how uncertainty creates a sense of separation or crowding in your concept.
steps: Open the built-in visual test. Keep its fixed settings unchanged.
Select each trial in order and watch for the same short period.
Write what visibly changes in each trial before adding an emotional interpretation.
experiments.observableEvidence: Record the visible arrangement, movement, or grouping. Note no visible difference if that is what you see.
experiments.technicalQuestion: What happens to the visible space between the shapes?
experiments.emotionalQuestion: Does the wide gap make you feel isolated, or does it offer breathing room? Feel free to disagree or see no connection.
experiments.constraintCheck: Use slow motion at a comfortable brightness. Stop if the display causes discomfort.

experiments.title: How much is enough?
experiments.researchQuestion: How does altering the number of slowly moving marks shift the visual weight of the composition?
experiments.conceptConnection: Changing the quantity of marks lets you explore how an overwhelming amount of detail relates to feelings of anxiety.
steps: Open the built-in visual test. Keep its fixed settings unchanged.
Select each trial in order and watch for the same short period.
Write what visibly changes in each trial before adding an emotional interpretation.
experiments.observableEvidence: Record the visible arrangement, movement, or grouping. Note no visible difference if that is what you see.
experiments.technicalQuestion: Which marks or groups are easiest to track in each trial?
experiments.emotionalQuestion: Do many marks feel chaotic, or just active? Let us know if this brings up a different feeling entirely.
experiments.constraintCheck: Use slow motion at a comfortable brightness. Stop if the display causes discomfort.

experiments.title: Time to notice
experiments.researchQuestion: How does varying the speed of continuous movement affect the overall tension of the display?
experiments.conceptConnection: Varying the pace helps examine how waiting or slow progression mirrors the unpredictability in your theme.
steps: Open the built-in visual test. Keep its fixed settings unchanged.
Select each trial in order and watch for the same short period.
Write what visibly changes in each trial before adding an emotional interpretation.
experiments.observableEvidence: Record the visible arrangement, movement, or grouping. Note no visible difference if that is what you see.
experiments.technicalQuestion: How does movement speed affect what you can follow?
experiments.emotionalQuestion: Does the slow movement feel calming or suspenseful to you? Tell us if you notice a different reaction.
experiments.constraintCheck: Use slow motion at a comfortable brightness. Stop if the display causes discomfort.
